title: A Model for Parts and Whole
objective: The Number Bond diagram (whole on top, two parts below) is a picture of the splitting/joining a learner already knows how to do with objects — not a new rule to learn.
studentQuestion: Can you show your object split using this picture instead?
newIdea: The NumberBond diagram as a representation of an already-understood action.

teaching.setup: 7 counters, already split into 5 and 2 as in prior lessons.
teaching.see: You already know 7 splits into 5 and 2. Here's a new way to draw that.
teaching.break: Map the physical whole and parts onto the diagram's three positions.
teaching.build: Draw/build the bond for 7 = 5 + 2 with the whole on top, parts below.
teaching.transform: The same split (7 into 5 and 2), shown as objects or as a bond diagram — same value, a new drawn form.

check.prompt: Cover the bond's whole and rebuild it from the two parts (objects), then reveal — does it match?

examples.transfer: A split the learner has already found themselves in Unit 0.2, redrawn as a bond without teacher demonstration.

mastery.evidence: Correctly draws a bond for a split already demonstrated with objects, twice.
